steps.title: Albariño
steps.body: Albariño is about 96% of Rías Baixas' vineyards. Its thick skins resist rot in the damp climate. It gives crisp, aromatic, dry whites with lemon, grapefruit, white peach, apricot and a saline, mineral edge. Wines labelled Rías Baixas Albariño must be 100% Albariño.

steps.title: Partners and styles
steps.body: In O Rosal and Condado do Tea, Albariño may be blended with Loureiro, floral, Treixadura, rounder, and Caíño Blanco. Most Albariño is fermented in steel and bottled young. Some producers age it on its lees for months or years, adding texture and allowing it to age; a few use oak. Rías Baixas also allows a little red wine.

steps.prompt: Match each term to Rías Baixas.

steps.body: Albariño aged on its lees for a year or more shows how serious it can be: creamy, saline and able to age five years or more.

steps.prompt: What must a Rías Baixas Albariño contain?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Albariño is about 96% of the vineyards
Its thick skins resist rot; it gives peach and salinity
Blends add Loureiro and Treixadura; lees ageing adds depth
